## Problem

For a given string `s`, determine the size of its longest subsequence that reads identically from left to right and right to left. The length of `s` will not exceed 1000.

### Input Specification
- Input contains only lowercase letters from the English alphabet.
- The input is the string `s`.

### Output Specification
- Output the length of the longest palindromic subsequence in `s`.

### Test Cases
- Input: `s = 'abca'`, Output: `3` (One longest palindromic subsequence is `'aba'`.)
- Input: `s = 'aebcbda'`, Output: `5` (One longest palindromic subsequence is `'abcba'`.)

### Example
```text
Input: racecar
Output: 7
```

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

This is a classic dynamic programming problem on subsequences, not substrings.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Define dp[i][j] as the length of the longest palindromic subsequence in the substring s[i..j], the recurrence depends on whether s[i] equals s[j].

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The time complexity should be O(n^2) and space can be optimized to O(n) using a 1D DP array.

</details>
